symbols.name: label space
symbols.meaning: The fixed space that contains every label, of dimension $m$.
symbols.quote: Fix a space $E$ of dimension $m$, the common space of all labels; here $m$ is that dimension, not the numerator of a dyadic rational.

symbols.name: label dimension
symbols.meaning: The dimension of the common space $E$, a count of the basis vectors of $E$; on the dyadic page $m$ means an integer numerator instead.
symbols.quote: Fix a space $E$ of dimension $m$, the common space of all labels; here $m$ is that dimension, not the numerator of a dyadic rational.

symbols.name: network vertex
symbols.meaning: A vertex of the network, a gate or a terminal, that carries a label.
symbols.quote: A vertex $w$ of the network, a gate or such a terminal, carries a label $L(w)$, a subspace of $E$.

symbols.name: vertex label
symbols.meaning: The label $L(w)$ of a vertex $w$, a subspace of $E$.
symbols.quote: A vertex $w$ of the network, a gate or such a terminal, carries a label $L(w)$, a subspace of $E$.

symbols.name: tail vertex
symbols.meaning: The vertex at which an edge starts.
symbols.quote: An edge runs from its tail $\sigma$ to its head $\tau$; these letters name vertices, not bank values.

symbols.name: head vertex
symbols.meaning: The vertex at which an edge ends.
symbols.quote: An edge runs from its tail $\sigma$ to its head $\tau$; these letters name vertices, not bank values.

symbols.name: label subspace
symbols.meaning: A subspace of $E$ used as the label of a gate or sink.
symbols.quote: Each gate or sink with label $U$, a subspace of $E$, is assigned $P_U$, the projection onto $U$ along its orthogonal complement $U^\perp$.

symbols.name: label projection
symbols.meaning: The projection onto the subspace $U$ along its orthogonal complement $U^\perp$.
symbols.quote: Each gate or sink with label $U$, a subspace of $E$, is assigned $P_U$, the projection onto $U$ along its orthogonal complement $U^\perp$.

symbols.name: smaller-call total
symbols.meaning: The total number of smaller calls, the sum of the drops over all edges; the letter changes meaning here and is not the route length of the frame page.
symbols.quote: Let $s$ be the total number of smaller calls, the sum of the drops over all edges.

relations.quote: The labels are built on a [Subset-intersection finite network](subset-network.md).
Each label sits at a gate or at a [Source, sink and terminal of a network](network-terminal.md).
The labels are chosen to make cheap the changes of [Frame of a vertex](frame.md) on each edge.
